newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks edge up in week on high volumes.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks edge up in week on high volumes.

text.p: Cyprus shares edged up 0.41 percent in the week ending June 27 amid increased volumes, profit taking, and a rally on shares in state carrier Cyprus Airways.
The Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) index, set at 100 points, closed the week at 76.82 points from last week's close of 76.50.

"Technical analysis this week continued pointing to a bullish market as the short term, 9 day-moving average is up. The fast moving average continues to be above the slow moving average issuing a signal for higher prices," said the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation CISCO in a weekly report.
Of the seven sub indices, four fell and three rose. Banking shares absorbed over 55 percent of the total weekly volumes of transactions.
Attention of the bourse was focused on shares in Cyprus Airways. The government has an 80 percent stake in the airline and the rest is traded on the exchange.
High demand for shares exhibited by an existing shareholder pushed its bid price through a fifteen percent volatility limit on Tuesday, resulting in automatic suspension of trade for one day.
Shares in the airline closed at 34.1 cents on Friday, a 3.9 percent rise from 32.8 cents last week, but still lower than the high of 40.4 cents reached before the bourse suspension on Tuesday.
Bank of Cyprus shares were trading at 295.5, steady on the share price of last week, while shares in the Cyprus Popular Bank dropped one cent to close at 306.5.
Fully paid Hellenic Bank shares gained four cents to close at 284.5.
Universal Life Insurance company closed the week with gains of 13 cents, at 471. Paneuropean Insurance shares were trading at 103.5 from 101.5 last Friday.
Blue chip cement stocks Vassiliko closed at 157.5, down two cents, and Cyprus Cement dipped 3.5 cents, closing at 244.5.
Beer and wine manufacturer KEO shares continued their upward trend of the past two weeks, gaining three cents and closing at 113.
